column5: Both pay a bonus for cards left undrawn in the deck at show end; Cut Act (a) bands the payout per five, Bench (a) pays per card - a numeric reskin of the same trigger/target/action.

Unopened Envelope (a) "every card never drawn by a show's end pays a bonus at that show's end" is the same effect as Bench (a) "a bonus per card left in the deck when the show ends" - undrawn deck cards paying out at show end.

Wild pip (a) "random rank and suit from those present on its row, updating every board change" is the same card as The Wildcard (a) "a copy of a rank and suit already present in its row" on every board change; Wildcard (b) "most common in row" also overlaps Wild pip (c) "most common in line, updating."

Birdman Race (b) "winning card holds a title granting a standing bonus until another card takes it" is the same seasonal-crown-contest effect as Seasonal Crown (a)+(b) "champion title carried until beaten, granting a standing bonus while held."

Double Booking (a) "two mutually exclusive objectives; finishing one voids the other" and Conflicting Notes (a) "two quests whose conditions cannot both hold; progress on one erases the other" describe the same simultaneous-mutually-exclusive-quest effect a player could not tell apart.

column4: Storyteller (a)/(b) (carry a portion of unspent score to next show's opening total, growing if unspent) overlap Griot (b)/(c), but Griot (a) adds a genuinely new re-fire-last-effect action Storyteller has no equivalent for; report but not a clean full duplicate.

Cut List (a card unplaced a whole show gains +1 rank permanently) and Uncalled Understudy (a card never placed a whole show upgrades permanently) share the same trigger, but "+1 rank" and a generic rarity "upgrade" may be genuinely different actions; unsure which the owner intends as distinct.

Quest-chain triggered stage acts (a) (a stage unlocks only after the previous one's effect triggers) is the same sequential-gating idea as The Three-Act Bill (a) (each objective visible/claimable only once the last is done), but one is the abstract structure pattern and the other a concrete three-stage instance; unsure if both were meant to stand.

Progress Report (a) (cue: reveal one hidden objective's exact progress at the cost of a placement) overlaps Silent Tally (c) (read progress once per show at the cost of a placement), differing mainly in scope (any hidden objective vs its own quest) and frequency; unsure if distinct enough.

Sealed Brief (progress bar visible from the start, identity hidden until completion) and Unspoken Brief (b) (objective reveals itself once mostly complete) both hide an objective's identity while surfacing some signal of progress; the exact reveal condition differs enough that the owner may want both.

Harlequin (a) (counts as both printed suits for every comparison/meld/prop) overlaps Split Costume (b) (carries two suits, counts as both at once, can be in two flushes), but Split Costume's other variants (context-dependent single suit) are not covered by Harlequin; report as an overlap, not a clean duplicate.

Dealt-Full Grid (a) and The Slider (a)/(b) both describe placing at an edge shoving a line one cell with the pushed-off card discarded, but Dealt-Full Grid is an always-on level default from a full board while The Slider is a skill card granting the shove at a full row/column; unsure if the owner wants the default rule and the grantable ability kept separate.
